name: Liver detox for yellow sclera

lead: Some appearance communities hold that yellowish or dull eye whites reflect a congested liver and can be whitened with a cleanse, herbs or supplements, giving brighter, whiter eyes.

Medical references describe yellowing of the white of the eye as scleral (conjunctival) icterus, caused by bilirubin depositing in the conjunctiva; it generally becomes visible at serum bilirubin of about 3 mg/dL or more. Causes are liver, blood or bile duct related. No study has tested a detox regimen for eye whiteness.

paras: Users follow cleanse diets, herbal blends or liver-support supplements for a period of days to weeks, often alongside cutting alcohol and eating more vegetables.

Yellow eyes, especially with yellow skin, can accompany hepatitis, cirrhosis, haemolysis or bile duct obstruction, and medical sources say they warrant evaluation. Detox products have not been studied for this purpose.

angle.text: Followers believe a liver cleanse relieves the liver and lets dull or yellowish eye whites clear. Medical sources link true yellowing to bilirubin, and no study has tested a detox for eye whiteness.

lead: Liver detox for yellow sclera is the practice of using cleansing diets, herbs, supplements or home liver cleanses with the aim of whitening yellowish or dull eye whites and giving the eyes a brighter, healthier look. Followers connect eye-white colour to liver health, and bright, clear whites are widely associated with a rested, healthy appearance.

Medical sources describe yellowing of the white of the eye as scleral icterus, a sign of jaundice. The pigment deposits in the conjunctiva, which has a high affinity for bilirubin, so it can appear before skin yellowing; visible conjunctival icterus generally indicates serum bilirubin of at least about 3 mg/dL. Causes are classed as prehepatic (excess red cell breakdown), hepatic (liver damage or inherited conjugation defects) and posthepatic (bile duct blockage).

Wikipedia's article on the sclera notes that eye-white colour also varies with age, skin tone and other conditions: fatty deposits can make the whites look slightly yellow in older adults, darker skin can have naturally darker sclerae, and irritation can redden them.[1] No published study has tested a detox regimen for eye whiteness.
infobox: Serum bilirubin of about 3 mg/dL or more

paras: Jaundice from high bilirubin usually involves the conjunctivae and diffuse yellowing of the skin. Carotenemia from large intakes of carotene-rich foods typically spares the conjunctivae and shows mainly on the palms and soles, and some drugs such as rifampin can yellow the skin without jaundice. Gilbert syndrome, found in about 5% of people, involves a less efficient bilirubin-processing enzyme with otherwise normal liver function and usually mild, stress-related jaundice. Medical references note that yellowing with yellow skin should be evaluated because it can signal liver, blood or bile duct disease.

Wikipedia's article on the sclera adds that jaundice produces yellow or light green tint, that conjunctivitis reddens the whites, and that some conditions such as osteogenesis imperfecta give a bluish tint.[1]

Detox diets and cleanses are described by Wikipedia as aiming to remove unspecified "toxins" through fasting, restrictive eating, herbs or similar practices.[2] Proponents say these practices release stored toxins that are then expelled in blood, skin, urine or stool.[2] The article reports that scientists and health bodies consider the concept unsupported, that a 2015 review found no convincing evidence that detox diets remove toxins, and that the liver and kidneys are the body's own detoxification system.[2] It also lists documented harms from some regimens, including cases of kidney injury and risks of prolonged fasting.[2]

On T Nation, members discuss liver cleanses such as lemon juice and olive oil, and coffee enemas, with some users reporting benefits and others citing Mayo Clinic warnings about harm.[3][4] One user wrote that a lemon-and-olive-oil cleanse improved his eye allergy symptoms.[3]

lore.intro: Liver-cleanse discussions on T Nation mention eye and allergy changes in passing; yellow sclera specifically is rarely discussed.[3][4]
